vision: Protocol-correct Aave V3 and V4 wrappers for Elixir — read positions, execute actions, and verify behavior against deployed contracts. Built on the onchain core library as part of the seven-repository onchain family.

actions_write.description: Aave V3 write surface: pool supply/borrow/repay/withdraw and the testnet faucet.

core_read.description: Aave V3 read surface: contract registry, math conversions, pool/oracle/ui-data reads, response type structs, multi-chain addresses.

event_error_decoding.description: Decode what the deployed protocol says back: Pool event logs with topic filters, structured revert reasons on write failures, and strict ABI decoding of responses.

math_validation.description: Cross-validate Aave.Math against Solidity (revm via onchain_evm) and Aave frontend math (@aave/math-utils via onchain_js).

multicall.description: Adopt Onchain.Multicall in Aave batch read paths where the protocol does not pre-batch.

v3_write_gaps.description: Close observed V3 position-management and reserve-read gaps, while removing protocol capabilities that deployed Aave no longer supports.

v4_support.description: Aave V4 Hub-and-Spoke support: address registry, read-surface selection, Hub/Spoke/Oracle/TokenizationSpoke reads, PositionManager writes, integration tests.

task.body: Port Aave V3's rayMul, rayDiv, wadMul, wadDiv, calculateLinearInterest, calculateCompoundedInterest from Solidity (aave-v3-core/contracts/protocol/libraries/math/) to Elixir. Preserve Aave's rounding semantics (half-up at the ray/wad midpoint — not trivial). Prerequisite for Task 41; the current Math module holds only trivial div_pow10 scale conversions with nothing worth oracle-validating.
task.implemented: Integer-native port of WadRayMath + MathUtils; source pinned to aave-v3-origin@1e3d70c. See CHANGELOG.md#task-40-port-aave-v3-wadraymath--mathutils-to-elixir.

task.title: Port missing WadRayMath ceil/floor variants on demand
task.body: rayMulFloor / rayMulCeil / rayDivFloor / rayDivCeil (from WadRayMath.sol) and mulDivCeil (from MathUtils.sol) exist in the pinned aave-v3-origin@1e3d70c source but aren't used by any Task 40 entrypoint, so Task 41's revm harness won't surface them as a gap. They ARE used by TokenMath.sol, ReserveLogic.sol, GenericLogic.sol, LiquidationLogic.sol. Gated until a caller from Pool/TokenMath call paths in this repo needs them; port minimally on demand with matching round-half-up semantics and revm cross-validation.

task.title: Cross-validate Aave.Math via revm against on-chain Aave V3
task.body: Repeat-with-revm cross-validation harness. Vendor a Solidity wrapper inlining Aave V3's 8 Layer-2 math function bodies verbatim from aave-v3-origin@1e3d70c; compile once with solc 0.8.10; inject runtime bytecode at a fake address via Onchain.EVM.simulate_call/3's state_overrides["code"]. For each function: deterministic vectors (zero, identity, midpoint rounding) plus StreamData random runs, assert bit-exact equality against Onchain.Aave.Math.
task.implemented: revm cross-validation harness with zero-tolerance equality across deterministic + StreamData property vectors for all 8 Layer-2 functions; SHA256-pinned compiled wrapper bytecode verified at setup_all. See CHANGELOG.md#task-41-revm-cross-validation-of-aavemath.

task.title: V4 math cross-validation via revm (V4 live on mainnet 2026-03-30)
task.body: V4 is live on Ethereum mainnet as of 2026-03-30. Repeat Task 41's harness against V4's math library: pin a mainnet block post-launch, call the V4 math contracts directly via Onchain.EVM.simulate_call/3, assert equality with a V4-specific Elixir port. Port V4-specific variants under Onchain.Aave.Math.V4 if V4's math diverged from V3. state_overrides["code"] bytecode injection is now a secondary fallback (for variants to test before mainnet exposure), not the primary path. task.title: Implement Onchain.Aave.V4.PositionManager ergonomic write wrappers (supply/borrow/repay analogs)
acceptance_criteria: Giver wrappers build `supplyOnBehalfOf` and `repayOnBehalfOf` calls, and Taker wrappers build `borrowOnBehalfOf` and `withdrawOnBehalfOf` calls, against the addresses resolved from `Onchain.Aave.Contracts`; unit tests assert the encoded selector and the full argument tuple for each.

The Taker allowance surface is wrapped: `approveBorrow`, `approveWithdraw`, `renounceBorrowAllowance`, `renounceWithdrawAllowance` as writes, and `borrowAllowance` / `withdrawAllowance` as reads, with decoding tests for the views.

Every wrapper takes the position owner as an explicit required argument and never substitutes the signer address for it. A test signs with one key and encodes a different `on_behalf_of`, asserting the owner in the calldata is the supplied one.

ABI shape is confirmed against the deployed contracts rather than assumed: at least one `@moduletag :integration` test issues a live `eth_call` against a Taker view (e.g. `borrowAllowance` or `BORROW_PERMIT_TYPEHASH`) on the mainnet archive node and asserts a decoded value, flunking with the required env vars when RPC is unavailable.

`InsufficientBorrowAllowance` and `InsufficientWithdrawAllowance` revert data is surfaced as a tagged error tuple carrying both the allowance and required amounts, not as raw hex; a unit test decodes each from its custom-error selector.
Invalid input is rejected before any RPC call: bad spoke/owner/spender addresses and a negative or non-integer amount return tagged error tuples, with tests.
`mix ci` is green, and `mix test.json --cover` reports at least 95% line coverage for the new module(s) — this is a money path per the critical-rules coverage tiers.
The new module(s) are registered in `OnchainAave.describe/0` (the discovery-manifest invariant test in `test/onchain_aave_test.exs` fails otherwise).
out_of_scope: Config Position Manager, Native Token Gateway, and Signature Gateway — separate surfaces (position configuration, ETH wrapping, EIP-712 intents); file a follow-on after this lands if they are wanted.
The `approveBorrowWithSig` / `approveWithdrawWithSig` EIP-712 permit variants on the Taker — they belong with the Signature Gateway work above.
Sending live V4 transactions on mainnet. Write paths are pinned by encoded-calldata unit tests; V4 has no Sepolia deployment (see Task 52, blocked on one).
task.body:
Primary user-facing write surface for V4. V4 has no `Pool`: supply/repay go through the Giver Position Manager (`:v4_giver_position_manager`) and borrow/withdraw through the Taker Position Manager (`:v4_taker_position_manager`), both already registered in `Onchain.Aave.Contracts`. Follow the V3 `Onchain.Aave.Pool` write convention (validate addresses, split network/signer opts, encode + sign + send) so the two trees read alike.

Verified against the provider-owned interfaces at https://github.com/aave/aave-v4 (`src/position-manager/interfaces/`) on 2026-08-21 — build against the deployed contracts, not against these notes:

- Giver: `supplyOnBehalfOf(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, uint256 amount, address onBehalfOf)` and `repayOnBehalfOf(...)`, same shape, both returning `(uint256, uint256)`.
- Taker: `borrowOnBehalfOf(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, uint256 amount, address onBehalfOf)` and `withdrawOnBehalfOf(...)`. The **caller** receives the assets and must already hold an allowance granted by `onBehalfOf`, so the allowance surface is part of this task, not a follow-on: `approveBorrow` / `approveWithdraw(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, address spender, uint256 amount)`, `renounceBorrowAllowance` / `renounceWithdrawAllowance(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, address owner)`, and the views `borrowAllowance` / `withdrawAllowance(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, address owner, address spender)`. Insufficient allowance reverts with the custom errors `InsufficientBorrowAllowance(uint256,uint256)` / `InsufficientWithdrawAllowance(uint256,uint256)`.

Two shape traps worth naming. First, V4 addresses a reserve by `uint256 reserveId` **scoped to a Spoke**, not by the asset address V3 used — the reserve id comes from the Spoke reads landed in Task 48, and passing an asset address where a reserve id belongs encodes silently and reverts on chain. Second, every entrypoint above is either `onBehalfOf`-parameterised or allowance-gated; none infers the position owner from `msg.sender`. That is what makes the Safe/DELEGATECALL constraint satisfiable, and it is also the thing an ergonomic wrapper is most likely to destroy by defaulting the owner to the signer address for convenience. Keep the owner an explicit, required argument on every wrapper.

task.title: Prove V4 reads and PositionManager writes against deployed mainnet state
acceptance_criteria: Pinned-block integration tests exercise representative Hub, Spoke, Oracle, and TokenizationSpoke reads against the deployed Ethereum contracts and assert domain values or cross-contract relationships, not only successful decoding
A pinned-mainnet-fork scenario executes PositionManager Giver supply and repay writes and asserts the corresponding Hub/Spoke accounting changes

A pinned-mainnet-fork scenario proves the Taker authorization boundary: borrow or withdraw without allowance returns the deployed Insufficient*Allowance error, then succeeds after the matching allowance is granted, with resulting position state asserted
Every live/fork test fails loudly with the required ETHEREUM_API_URL setup when the archive RPC is unavailable; no missing-environment skip path exists
The integration test modules record the pinned block, deployed contract addresses, observed success semantics, and observed relevant error semantics
mix ci passes, and mix test.json --quiet --include integration passes with the archive RPC available
task.body:
Close the independent-evidence gap for the shipped V4 wrappers. The current suite primarily proves calldata and decoding against stubs; one live PositionManager allowance read exists, but no state-changing V4 wrapper is exercised end to end.

Use the deployed Ethereum V4 contracts as the semantic authority. Pin all live and forked calls to a named block so configuration changes cannot turn exact-value assertions into noise. Reads must cover the Hub/Spoke accounting relationships selected by Tasks 47–50 and 57. Writes must exercise both sides of PositionManager: Giver accounting for supply/repay and Taker allowance enforcement for borrow/withdraw.

The former Sepolia blocker is obsolete. Aave launched a public Tenderly-based V4 testnet on 2025-11-19, and V4 is now deployed on Ethereum mainnet. More importantly, onchain_evm can execute stateful writes against pinned mainnet state; test/onchain/aave/simulation_integration_test.exs proves that mechanism against Aave V3. A testnet lifecycle is therefore not an authority or availability dependency for this task.

AUTHORITY: live deployed traffic plus Aave-owned V4 source, deployment documentation, and interfaces. Stubs and captured payloads remain regression fixtures only; they do not grade deployed semantics.
task.implemented: Pinned-block (25800000) live reads assert Hub/Spoke/Oracle/TokenizationSpoke WETH accounting relationships, and a signed-wrapper mainnet fork covers Giver supply/repay Hub/Spoke deltas plus the Taker InsufficientBorrowAllowance(0, 1e18) boundary followed by approve+borrow with position state asserted. test/onchain/aave/v4/deployed_integration_test.exs; no skip path (RPCCase.rpc_url! flunks). Reviewer additionally bumped onchain_evm to 0.6 in cffc83e — 0.5.1 clobbers unfetched WETH code under fetch-before-amend overrides.

task.title: Onchain.Aave.DebtToken — wrap approveDelegation + borrowAllowance on variable/stable debt tokens
task.body:
Aave V3 credit delegation (approveDelegation(delegatee, amount) on the variable/stable debt token) lets a position owner grant another address the right to Pool.borrow(..., onBehalfOf=owner) against the owner's collateral. Observed on-chain 2026-04-22 — a real migration-off-automation flow the current write surface doesn't support.

Onchain.Aave.Pool covers supply/borrow/repay/withdraw but the delegation mechanism lives on the debt-token contract, not Pool. Build a thin wrapper exposing approve_delegation/4 (write) and borrow_allowance/3 (read) against the variable and stable debt token addresses. Debt-token addresses come from Pool.getReserveData(asset).variableDebtTokenAddress / .stableDebtTokenAddress — consider a helper that resolves (asset, rate_mode) → debt_token_address. Integration test on Sepolia mirroring pool_write_integration_test shape.

Context observed 2026-04-22 (same Safe, end-to-end USDC→USDS debt swap): three user-signed approveDelegation txs each to a different counterfactual CREATE2 adapter (Aave's UI re-derives the salt per session/amount, so allowances are not reusable). Implications: (a) approve_delegation/4 is the 80% feature; (b) zero-out revocation (approve_delegation(debt_token, delegatee, 0, …)) is mandatory hygiene — incomplete sessions leave dangling allowances to dead CREATE2 addresses; (c) a future helper could wrap "revoke all orphan delegations on a debt token for this account" by scanning BorrowAllowanceDelegated logs — nice-to-have, not core.

task.title: Mine defi-skills:intent-to-transaction action surface for onchain_aave coverage gaps
acceptance_criteria: A 'Proposed additions from defi-skills mining' section lands in this roadmap listing each candidate task with D/B/U scores, the corresponding defi-skills action(s), and a coverage-status note (already-covered / partial / gap)
User merges accepted entries into V3 Write Surface Gaps
out_of_scope: Any Onchain.Aave.* code edits — read-only discovery + scoring only
task.body:
Planted 2026-04-30 from a cartouche session surveying cross-repo applicability of the defi-skills skill. Self-contained discovery exercise — execute from a fresh onchain_aave Claude Code session so this repo's CLAUDE.md, hooks, and Aave V3 fixtures are loaded.

Prompt for the executing session: Invoke /defi-skills:intent-to-transaction to load the skill, then run `defi-skills actions --json` to enumerate the supported action surface (~50 actions across Aave, Uniswap, Lido, Compound, Balancer, Pendle, EigenLayer, Curve, MakerDAO, Rocket Pool, Fibrous, WETH). Map relevant actions to onchain_aave's scope: direct parity with defi-skills' 7 aave_* actions — aave_supply, aave_withdraw, aave_borrow, aave_repay, aave_set_collateral, aave_repay_with_atokens, aave_claim_rewards. For each, check whether Onchain.Aave.* already covers it (read calldata-construction details from the action's JSON spec, compare against Onchain.Aave.Pool / sibling modules); flag any gap as a candidate roadmap entry. Also note V3 Pool functions exposed by defi-skills we don't model yet (interest-rate-mode toggling, eMode category selection, repay-with-permit). For each gap, propose a roadmap entry with D/B/U scoring. Read-only — discovery + scoring only, no code edits. The skill is already installed (pip install defi-skills); no new deps. Companion tasks were planted in hieroglyph, onchain, and onchain_evm ROADMAPs the same day.
task.implemented: Mined the defi-skills 0.3.0 action surface (53 actions, 7 aave_v3) via four parallel subagents, each verifying signatures against the deployed mainnet Pool and aave-dao/aave-v3-origin rather than against defi-skills. Coverage: withdraw/borrow/repay covered; supply covered except the caller-side approve pre-step; set_collateral, repay_with_atokens and claim_rewards are gaps. Findings that removed work: swapBorrowRateMode is gone from IPool since v3.2 (live call reverts), and the deployed UiPoolDataProvider.getEModes returns the six-field v3.3 EModeCategory while aave-v3-origin/main declares eight — decoding against the source branch buffer-overruns. Accepted candidates merged into V3 Write Surface Gaps as tasks 58 (eMode), 59 (direct reserve reads, debt-token resolution by getter, retirement of the dead stable-rate paths) and 60 (setUserUseReserveAsCollateral, repayWithATokens). Declined: supply-with-approval orchestration (caller policy, would need a per-token USDT reset constant), the bitmap and packed-config reads (UiPoolDataProvider decodes them already), flashLoan (caller must deploy a receiver), governance functions. Held: a Rewards module (all sampled mainnet distributions are expired) and liquidationCall. Deferred cross-repo: supplyWithPermit/repayWithPermit, blocked on ERC-2612 signing absent from onchain core.

task.title: Mutation-grade Aave V3/V4 math differential suite
acceptance_criteria: Property domains cover every public V3/V4 math operation across zero, unit, boundary, overflow-adjacent and rounding-sensitive inputs
Results are differential-checked against pinned official Aave Solidity math compiled to exact bytecode and executed through onchain_evm/revm
A reproducible mutation campaign exercises arithmetic operators, comparisons, clamps and rounding directions; every survivor is classified with evidence
A deliberately wrong rounding/boundary implementation is caught by the suite and fails the verification run
The ledger records Aave source authority, compiler settings, bytecode hashes, mutator/tool versions and survivor review; critical touched modules remain at least 95% covered and mix ci passes
task.body: Turn the existing V3/V4 unit, integration and revm checks into an adequacy-tested financial-math oracle. The official Aave contracts and observed deployed semantics define the formulas; locally compiled reference bytecode is evidence only when its source, compiler settings and hashes are pinned. Grade the suite with generated and domain mutations so a shared wrong constant, rounding direction or boundary assumption cannot be ratified by matching fixtures.

Onchain.Aave.V4.Hub exposes IHub MAX_ALLOWED_UNDERLYING_DECIMALS, MIN_ALLOWED_UNDERLYING_DECIMALS, MAX_ALLOWED_SPOKE_CAP, and MAX_RISK_PREMIUM_THRESHOLD

task.body:

- IHubBase previewAdd/Remove/Draw/Restore ByAssets and ByShares (eight functions). These are the Hub share-to-asset converters used before add/remove/draw/restore; rounding direction differs per action (documented on each function in IHubBase.sol).

task.title: Onchain.Aave.Pool — eMode: setUserEMode, getUserEMode, category config, and enumeration via getEModes
acceptance_criteria: Pool.set_user_e_mode/2 (plus a ! variant) encodes setUserEMode(uint8) and sends through the module's existing signed-write path
Pool.get_user_e_mode/2 returns the user's active category id from a pinned-block live archive read
Pool.get_e_mode_category_collateral_config/2 returns ltv, liquidation threshold and liquidation bonus as Decimal ratios via Math.to_ltv/1

UiPoolDataProvider.get_e_modes/2 decodes the deployed Emode[] wrapper as {uint8 id, seven-field EModeCategory}; a pinned-block integration test asserts category 1 id, ltv 0.93, liquidation threshold 0.95, bonus 1.01, label "ETH correlated", and ltvzeroBitmap
A decode regression test includes a category whose ltvzeroBitmap is non-zero, proving that neither the wrapper id nor the deployed seventh field can be silently discarded
%Onchain.Aave.Types.EModeCategory{} includes the category id and every deployed inner field, with a doctest matching sibling type conventions
A pinned-mainnet-fork test changes a user's eMode through setUserEMode, reads the changed category back, and pins the relevant deployed error for an invalid category
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: swapBorrowRateMode — removed from IPool in v3.2, reverts on the deployed contract
getEModeCategoryData(uint8) legacy struct and the four category bitmap getters
setUserEModeOnBehalfOf and the v3.5 position-manager delegation surface
Any Aave V4 eMode equivalent
task.body:
eMode is one of the remaining user-facing position controls missing from `Onchain.Aave.Pool`. Without it a caller cannot switch a position into a configured efficiency category, so the package cannot express the borrowing-power configuration used by correlated-asset positions.

Add the write `setUserEMode(uint8)` and the reads `getUserEMode(address)` and `getEModeCategoryCollateralConfig(uint8)` to `Pool`, following the existing `send_pool_tx` / `Contract.call` patterns in that module. Add category enumeration through `UiPoolDataProvider.getEModes(address)`, which returns every category in one call and is the better shape than looping `getEModeCategoryData(uint8)` per id. Introduce an `EModeCategory` struct in `lib/onchain/aave/types/` alongside the existing types, converting ltv / liquidation threshold / bonus through `Onchain.Aave.Math.to_ltv/1` so they read like every other ratio in this library.

DECODE HAZARD — verified against the deployed mainnet UiPoolDataProvider at 0x56b7A1012765C285afAC8b8F25C69Bf10ccfE978 on 2026-08-23. `getEModes` returns `Emode[]`: every array entry wraps `uint8 id` plus a SEVEN-field EModeCategory `(uint16 ltv, uint16 liquidationThreshold, uint16 liquidationBonus, uint128 collateralBitmap, string label, uint128 borrowableBitmap, uint128 ltvzeroBitmap)`. A six-field decoder can silently discard the final word, while current aave-v3-origin source declares an additional `isolated` field not present in this deployed helper. Pin the deployed seven-field contract at a fixed block and keep the wrapper id load-bearing.

BLOCK FLOOR — independently re-verified 2026-08-23 against the local archive node. `getEModes` returns EMPTY calldata below block 24033627 (the helper's deployment); the repo's existing integration tests pin 21000000, where this call yields zero bytes. Pin the eMode tests at a block at or above 24033627 and make an empty return a hard failure, never an empty category list. At block 25800000 the call returns 48 categories: id 1 is (9300, 9500, 10100, 2952790659, "ETH correlated", 1, 0), and the only categories with a non-zero ltvzeroBitmap are id 3 ("rsETH__ETH_wstETH_ETHx") and id 42 ("rsETH__USDC_USDT"), both 68719476736 — use one of those two for the regression test rather than searching for a candidate.

Related: `getEModeCategoryData(uint8)` still exists and still returns the legacy struct with a dead always-zero `priceSource`; prefer `getEModeCategoryCollateralConfig(uint8)` for the live ltv/lt/bonus and treat the legacy getter as out of scope. `swapBorrowRateMode(address,uint256)` was removed from IPool with the v3.2 stable-rate deprecation and reverts on the deployed mainnet Pool — do not model it (verified live 2026-08-23; training data still carries it).

task.title: Retire stable-rate APIs and resolve variable debt tokens through the dedicated Pool getter
acceptance_criteria: Pool.get_reserve_variable_debt_token/2 decodes getReserveVariableDebtToken(address); a pinned-block integration test asserts the deployed mainnet WETH variable debt-token address
DebtToken.debt_token_address/3 resolves :variable through Pool.get_reserve_variable_debt_token/2, with no getReserveData tuple decode or positional debt-token indexing left in DebtToken

Pool.borrow/4, Pool.repay/4, and DebtToken.debt_token_address/3 reject :stable locally as {:error, {:unsupported_interest_rate_mode, :stable}} before any RPC or signing call; bang variants raise with the same tagged reason
A pinned-mainnet-fork scenario establishes a borrowable position and records the deployed protocol rejection for interest-rate mode 1, independently confirming the local public-API rejection
Public docs and types expose only the variable mode, and CHANGELOG records the :stable removal as a breaking change with its protocol-level reason
Existing variable-mode unit, live-read, and write integration behavior remains green
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: The typed getReserveData surface and normalized reserve-index reads — tracked separately
getConfiguration / getUserConfiguration packed bitmaps
Any Aave V4 module
task.body:
Remove a public capability that deployed Aave no longer supports and eliminate the fragile tuple-position dependency used to select debt tokens. Aave's current ValidationLogic accepts only `DataTypes.InterestRateMode.VARIABLE`; the deployed Pool still returns a vestigial stable-debt-token address, but that address does not make stable borrowing a supported operation.

The public contract is explicit: `:variable` remains supported and `:stable` returns `{:error, {:unsupported_interest_rate_mode, :stable}}` before RPC or signing. Apply that behavior consistently to Pool borrow/repay and DebtToken address resolution, including bang variants and documentation. This is a deliberate breaking correction, not a reviewer-selected policy.

`DebtToken.debt_token_address/3` currently decodes the full 15-field `getReserveData(address)` response and selects a positional slot. Replace that dependency with the deployed `getReserveVariableDebtToken(address)` getter exposed through Pool, preserving the independently observed mainnet address.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Ethereum Pool at 0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2 plus aave-dao/aave-v3-origin IPool and ValidationLogic. Prove one live variable-token success and the relevant mode-1 protocol rejection on a pinned fork before encoding the local behavior.

task.title: Onchain.Aave.Pool — setUserUseReserveAsCollateral and repayWithATokens
acceptance_criteria: Pool.set_user_use_reserve_as_collateral/3 and its ! variant encode setUserUseReserveAsCollateral(address,bool) and send through the module's existing signed-write path
Pool.repay_with_atokens/3 and its ! variant encode repayWithATokens(address,uint256,uint256) with rate mode fixed internally at 2 and no on_behalf_of argument
Unit tests assert encoded calldata against selectors 0x5a3b74b9 and 0x2dad97d4, not merely that a call was attempted

A pinned-mainnet-fork scenario supplies collateral, toggles its collateral usage, and asserts the resulting user configuration; disabling collateral when it would violate the position constraints pins the deployed error semantics

A pinned-mainnet-fork scenario establishes variable debt and an aToken balance, repays through repayWithATokens, and asserts both debt and aToken balance changes; a no-debt call pins the relevant deployed error
Both functions carry Descripex api() blocks and moduledoc table entries matching the module's conventions

out_of_scope: setUserUseReserveAsCollateralOnBehalfOf and the v3.5 position-manager delegation surface
repayWithPermit — blocked on ERC-2612 permit signing, which onchain core does not yet provide
liquidationCall
Any Aave V4 module
task.body:
Add two Aave V3 Pool writes that close distinct position-management gaps. Both reuse the module's signed-write boundary, while their acceptance depends on real state transitions rather than calldata alone.

`setUserUseReserveAsCollateral(address asset, bool useAsCollateral)` — selector 0x5a3b74b9, confirmed against the deployed mainnet Pool. This is how a caller stops an asset from backing debt without withdrawing it. Today the library can supply an asset but cannot un-collateralize it, so a user isolating risk across positions has no path through this package at all.

`repayWithATokens(address asset, uint256 amount, uint256 interestRateMode) returns (uint256)` — selector 0x2dad97d4. It takes no `onBehalfOf` and repays for `msg.sender`. Fix the internal mode at the only deployed supported value, `2`; do not expose a rate-mode option.

The `type(uint256).max` convention works transparently for full repayment: Elixir's arbitrary-precision integers pass 2^256 - 1 straight through and the Pool contract interprets it, so no client-side special-casing is needed — document it in the parameter docs the way `withdraw/4` already does.

AUTHORITY: signatures from the deployed mainnet Pool (0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2) and aave-dao/aave-v3-origin `src/contracts/interfaces/IPool.sol`. https://aave.com/docs is stale in places — it still documents functions absent from current IPool. Probe the deployed contract rather than asserting from memory.

acceptance_criteria: Pool.get_reserve_data/2 returns %Onchain.Aave.Types.ReserveData{} whose 15 fields and numeric widths match the deployed getReserveData(address) ABI at a pinned Ethereum block

ReserveData preserves configuration, liquidity and debt indices/rates, timestamp, reserve id, token addresses, accruedToTreasury, unbacked, and isolationModeTotalDebt; docs explicitly identify currentStableBorrowRate, stableDebtTokenAddress, interestRateStrategyAddress, unbacked, and isolationModeTotalDebt as deployed compatibility fields with deprecated semantics

getReservesCount, getReserveAddressById, flash-loan premium constants, and registry introspection getters

task.body:
Expose the deployed Pool reserve data needed to reconcile scaled balances and inspect reserve state without routing through the broader UI data provider. This task follows Task 59 so the variable-debt-token getter already has one owner and is reused here.

getReserveData(address) returns a 15-field compatibility struct: configuration; liquidity index; current liquidity rate; variable borrow index; current variable borrow rate; current stable borrow rate; last-update timestamp; reserve id; aToken, stable-debt-token, variable-debt-token, and interest-rate-strategy addresses; accrued-to-treasury; unbacked; and isolation-mode total debt. Preserve the deployed layout exactly, while documenting which fields remain only for compatibility and no longer represent supported stable-rate or bridge behavior.

Add the direct aToken and normalized income/debt index reads needed by consumers of scaled reserve/user balances. Prove the semantic relationship at one pinned block by reconstructing both aToken and variable-debt balances and comparing them with the token contracts' own balanceOf results.

task.title: Make the integration gate settle: bound math_revm runtime so --include integration terminates
acceptance_criteria: mix test.json --include integration terminates on a healthy archive node and reports a summary, with the wall-clock ceiling stated in the test module or CLAUDE.md
An unreachable or mid-run-dropped archive RPC fails the affected math_revm test loudly within a bounded time instead of hanging; no test retains timeout: :infinity
The revm cross-validation still fails on a real divergence — a deliberately wrong expected value in one deterministic vector makes that test red
The chosen coverage/runtime tradeoff is recorded in the test module's moduledoc, including how to run the exhaustive variant
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Funding the Sepolia key or fixing the four sepolia_send tests that fail with rpc -32003
Changing Onchain.Aave.Math itself or its Solidity wrapper bytecode
Reworking harness' progress-stall reflex
task.body:
`mix test.json --include integration` does not terminate under any practical time cap, which makes the repo's own live gate unusable for dispatched agents and for CI.

Evidence, all from 2026-08-23: harness run-1787478012579-900e9275 was killed by the progress-stall reflex while idle-waiting on this suite, and its transcript shows the agent had its own module green and was blocked solely on the gate. The reviewer of run-1787481036522-9e92c0d9 recorded `Did not finish in 17m (0% CPU, ~27MB RSS, DirtyIo NIF ESTABLISHED to 127.0.0.1:8545)`, plus SIGALRM 142 at 90s on `--only math_revm` and at 120s on `--only integration --exclude math_revm`, and fell back to running the suite file-by-file. A local full run of test/onchain/aave/math_revm_test.exs alone took 3055 seconds.

Two compounding causes: the math_revm modules set `timeout: :infinity`, and `Onchain.EVM` calls run on a DirtyIo scheduler, so ExUnit cannot interrupt a stalled archive fetch — a flapping node turns into an unbounded hang rather than a failure. Independently, every property does `max_runs` live fork calls, so the wall-clock cost is inherently large even when the node is healthy.

Give the suite a bounded, interruptible runtime without giving up the cross-validation guarantee that makes `Onchain.Aave.Math` trustworthy. Decide and document the coverage/runtime tradeoff explicitly rather than silently shrinking the property space: options include a finite per-test timeout, a smaller default `max_runs` with an opt-in exhaustive mode, reusing one fork across vectors instead of one per call, or separating the revm cross-validation into its own tag that the ordinary integration gate does not pull in. Whatever is chosen, `--include integration` must terminate and a dead or flapping RPC must surface as a loud failure, never as a hang.

task.title: Decode deployed Aave V3 Pool events from logs with topic-filter fetch
acceptance_criteria: An events module decodes the deployed V3 Pool's protocol events — at minimum Supply, Withdraw, Borrow, Repay, LiquidationCall, FlashLoan and ReserveDataUpdated — from raw log maps into named-field maps, with event signatures and indexed layouts taken from Aave-owned IPool source, not from a third-party client

A pinned-block integration test fetches real mainnet Pool logs via Onchain.RPC.eth_get_logs against the archive node and decodes them, asserting known field values of at least one historical Supply and one LiquidationCall log; missing RPC env vars flunk with exact export instructions

Topic-filter construction produces eth_getLogs topics for an event with optional indexed-argument filters, and the integration test round-trips one filter: build it, fetch live, and every returned log decodes as that event
Indexed reference-type parameters surface as their topic hash and the behavior is documented
Unit tests pin decoding against log fixtures recorded from the live observations

out_of_scope: Aave V4 Hub/Spoke event decoding
Streaming/subscription (eth_subscribe) support and any indexer or backfill machinery
aToken/debt-token ERC-20 Transfer logs — Onchain.Transfer already owns token transfer decoding
task.body:
onchain_aave has no event surface: nothing reads or decodes the logs the protocol emits, so a consumer can execute a supply or borrow through this library but cannot observe its effect — or anyone else's activity — from the chain. Add log decoding for the deployed V3 Pool's event set plus topic-filter construction for eth_getLogs.

The in-family precedent is Onchain.Transfer: it fetches with Onchain.RPC.eth_get_logs and decodes per-event with Onchain.Log.decode_event/2 against signature strings with indexed markers (verified by reading onchain core, 2026-08-25). For building topic filters with indexed-argument values, hieroglyph provides ABI.encode_event_topics/2 — hieroglyph is already in the dependency tree transitively; if it is used directly, declare it as a direct dependency rather than reaching through onchain's tree undeclared.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Ethereum Pool at 0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2 and Aave-owned aave-v3-origin IPool event definitions. Establish each event's signature and indexed layout from that source and prove decoding against real mainnet logs at pinned blocks before deriving fixtures; third-party ABIs and explorers are reference material only.

Dispatch trigger: public API addition with live external-system evidence against the archive node.

task.title: Surface decoded revert reasons on Aave write and call failures
acceptance_criteria: A revert blob returned by the library's call/estimate/send paths decodes through hieroglyph's built-in Error(string)/Panic(uint256) recognition and, where the deployed protocol emits custom errors, through Aave-owned error definitions; the decoded reason appears in the returned error tuple

Which revert style the deployed V3 Pool and the V4 deployment actually emit is established live and recorded — a pinned-fork failing write (e.g. borrow exceeding collateral capacity) pins the raw blob and its decoded form for each protocol generation

V3 numeric error-code strings map to their Aave-owned Errors.sol names in the surfaced reason, with the mapping generated from or verified against aave-v3-origin source rather than transcribed from memory
Existing error-tuple shapes remain matchable by current consumers, or the shape change is recorded in CHANGELOG as a breaking change with the migration
The hand-defined allowance-error decode in the V4 position manager routes through the same shared decode path instead of a module-local table
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Retry or error-classification policy on top of decoded reasons
Event/log decoding — its own task
onchain core changes — its decode_error surface is consumed as-is
task.body:
Today exactly one call site decodes a revert: the V4 position manager matches its two hand-defined allowance errors (lib/onchain/aave/v4/position_manager.ex:284). Every other write and simulated call returns the revert payload as an opaque rpc_error blob, so a consumer learns "execution reverted" but not why — on a money path that is the difference between a diagnosable rejection and a dead end.

hieroglyph decodes the two Solidity built-ins Error(string) and Panic(uint256) with no definitions supplied (since 1.5.0), and accepts error definitions for custom errors. Aave V3 validation historically reverts with numeric string codes defined in Errors.sol ("51" and the like) — premise unverified for the currently deployed Pool: establish live which style each protocol generation actually emits before encoding any mapping. Route all Aave write/call revert paths through one shared decode step that yields a structured reason.

AUTHORITY: the deployed contracts — pinned-fork failing writes provide the live error evidence — and Aave-owned aave-v3-origin / V4 sources for error definitions and code-to-name mappings.

Dispatch trigger: money-path error surface with live external-system evidence.

task.title: Adopt strict ABI decoding across Aave response decode paths
acceptance_criteria: The uniform-strict vs opt-in decision is made and recorded in the affected moduledocs, and the chosen behavior is implemented across the library's response decode paths
A hand-built non-canonical response (trailing bytes, dirty padding) surfaces as a tagged decode error from a representative read function, asserted by unit test

Live pinned-block integration reads across the V3 and V4 surfaces stay green under strict decoding, confirming deployed protocol responses are canonical — or the finding that they are not is recorded and the approach revised
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Changing onchain core's decode surface — onchain task 88 owns that
Event and revert decoding — their own tasks
task.body:
Blocked on onchain core exposing decode options: Onchain.ABI.decode_response/2 and Onchain.Contract.call currently accept none (verified by reading onchain core, 2026-08-25), so hieroglyph's strict mode cannot be reached from this repo. Once onchain task 88 lands, turn it on for this library's own decodes.

Every byte this package decodes comes from an RPC endpoint the consumer configured but does not control, and responses from deployed Aave contracts are canonical ABI — a payload that fails strict decoding is corrupt or hostile, and today it decodes permissively and silently. Verify the canonicality premise against live pinned-block reads across the V3 and V4 surfaces before committing to uniform strict; record the outcome either way.

Routing is left open on purpose: the change is small but its cost depends on how core task 88 shapes the options surface. Decide assignee/model when this unblocks.
task.blocked_reason: onchain task 88 must land first: Onchain.ABI.decode_response/2 and Onchain.Contract.call accept no decode options today, so strict mode is unreachable from this repo

task.title: Execute the V4 Tokenization Spoke: ERC-4626 writes and the share token's ERC-20 surface
acceptance_criteria: Whether the deployed share token exposes an executable ERC-20 surface — transfer, approve, allowance, EIP-2612 permit — and under what restrictions is established live against a deployed Tokenization Spoke and recorded in the moduledoc; the wrapper surfaces what exists and documents what does not

deposit, mint, withdraw and redeem execute against a pinned-block mainnet fork and move both share balance and underlying balance in the direction and magnitude the matching preview_* read predicted, within the documented rounding direction
A share transfer between two accounts is exercised on the fork and both balances reflect it, or the finding that transfers are restricted is recorded with the on-chain evidence for that restriction
Each new write is pinned by an encoded-calldata unit test asserting the 4-byte selector and argument encoding, matching the existing V4 position-manager test pattern
Share-token reads route through Onchain.ERC20 rather than module-local call_uint reimplementations, or the moduledoc records why they cannot
Missing RPC or fork prerequisites flunk with the exact export commands, never skip
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Hub-level writes and the Hub/Spoke configurators
IConfigPositionManager and ISpoke position-manager authorization — its own task
Off-chain APY or share-price timeseries derivation
task.body:
The Tokenization Spoke is the one V4 object other protocols can hold: an ERC-4626 share per (Hub, asset), which is what makes a V4 supply position portable into a vault, a lending market, or trading collateral elsewhere. This library can currently only look at it. lib/onchain/aave/v4/tokenization_spoke.ex is read-only — the ERC-4626 previews and caps are wrapped (preview_deposit/preview_mint/preview_withdraw/preview_redeem, max_*), the EIP-712 typehashes and domain separator are readable, but there is no deposit, mint, withdraw or redeem, and the share token exposes only balance_of/2 and total_supply/1 — no transfer, approve, allowance or executable permit. A consumer can compute what a deposit would mint and cannot make the deposit.

Premise unverified — confirm before building on it: that the deployed share token is a freely transferable ERC-20 with working EIP-2612 permit. It is inferred from the permit typehash and domain-separator getters this module already reads, not from an on-chain observation; a Spoke share could be transfer-restricted while a position is used as collateral. Establish the real behavior first and let the finding shape the wrapper, rather than shipping a transfer wrapper that reverts.

Onchain.ERC20 (onchain dep) already provides balance_of/allowance/decimals/symbol/total_supply/approve/transfer and is the established pattern in this repo's V3 write integration tests. Prefer delegating to it over reimplementing token reads locally.

The four signed-intent typehashes this module reads (deposit/mint/withdraw/redeem) suggest a signature path exists alongside the direct calls; wrap the direct calls here and record what the intent path would additionally require.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Ethereum Tokenization Spokes registered in Onchain.Aave.Contracts and Aave-owned aave-v4 ITokenizationSpoke source. Fork execution at a pinned block is the evidence for every write; previews and third-party ABIs are reference material only.

Dispatch trigger: money-path write surface requiring live external-system evidence.

task.title: Wrap V4 position configuration and position-manager authorization, and close the Taker fork-evidence gap
acceptance_criteria: A user can authorize and revoke a position manager on a Spoke and toggle a reserve's collateral flag through this library's public API, without hand-encoding calldata

The Config Position Manager's on-behalf-of configuration surface is wrapped with the owner as an explicit required argument, consistent with the Giver/Taker wrappers' rule that no entrypoint infers the owner from msg.sender
withdraw, approve_withdraw and both renounce_* paths are exercised on a pinned-block mainnet fork with balance and allowance assertions, not only by calldata-shape unit tests
A withdraw attempted beyond the granted allowance fails on the fork and surfaces the tagged insufficient_withdraw_allowance tuple carrying allowance and required amount
Each new write is pinned by an encoded-calldata unit test asserting the 4-byte selector and argument encoding
The raw encoded_call usages in the V4 deployed integration test are replaced by the new wrappers
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: INativeTokenGateway and ISignatureGateway
The governance surfaces: IHubConfigurator, ISpokeConfigurator, IAaveV4ConfigEngine, IAccessManagerEnumerable
Tokenization Spoke ERC-4626 writes — its own task
task.body:
V4's delegation surface is what makes a position programmable — Aave ships the three Position Managers explicitly so third-party contracts can act on a position without governance listing, gated by per-reserve allowances the user grants and can revoke. This library wraps only two thirds of it, and one gap blocks ordinary use: there is no way to enable a position manager or to toggle a reserve as collateral. IConfigPositionManager has zero coverage, and ISpoke's setUserPositionManager / setUsingAsCollateral are reachable today only by hand-encoding — the V4 deployed integration test calls them through raw encoded_call rather than through Spoke (verified 2026-08-26 by reading test/onchain/aave/v4/deployed_integration_test.exs and grepping lib/ for the interface names).

The second half of this task closes an evidence gap on a money path already shipped: of the Taker surface, supply, approve_borrow, borrow and repay are exercised on a fork at a pinned mainnet block, but withdraw, approve_withdraw and the renounce_* counterparts are pinned only by calldata-shape unit tests against an RPC stub. A selector assertion proves the call encodes; it does not prove the deployed contract moves the assets or enforces the allowance. Both halves live in the same module and the same fork test, so they are one session's work.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Ethereum V4 Spokes and Position Managers registered in Onchain.Aave.Contracts, plus Aave-owned aave-v4 ISpoke / IConfigPositionManager / ITakerPositionManager source. Fork execution at a pinned block is the evidence; the existing stub tests are reference material only.

Dispatch trigger: authorization and money-path write surface requiring live external-system evidence.

task.title: Decode V4 Hub, Spoke and Tokenization Spoke events from logs
acceptance_criteria: The V4 protocol events actually emitted by the deployed Hubs, Spokes and Tokenization Spokes are enumerated from Aave-owned aave-v4 source and each is decoded from a raw log map into a named-field map

A pinned-block integration test fetches real mainnet V4 logs via Onchain.RPC.eth_get_logs and decodes them, asserting known field values of at least one Hub credit-line event, one Spoke position event and one ERC-4626 Deposit or Withdraw; missing RPC env vars flunk with exact export instructions
Topic-filter construction scopes a fetch to one Spoke or one Hub asset, and every log the filter returns decodes as the expected event
Spoke-local reserveId values in decoded events are resolvable to their underlying asset through the existing Spoke reads, and the moduledoc shows that path
Decoding shares the module and conventions task 63 establishes for V3 rather than forking a parallel implementation
Unit tests pin decoding against log fixtures recorded from the live observations
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: V3 Pool events — task 63 owns them
Streaming via eth_subscribe, and any indexer, backfill or storage machinery
Revert decoding — task 64 owns it
task.body:
Nothing in this library can observe what V4 did. The wrappers can read current Hub and Spoke state and execute writes, but there is no way to see a supply, a borrow, a liquidation, a credit-line draw or a share mint after the fact — and V4 makes that gap worse than it was in V3, because state that used to be one Pool's is now spread across three Hubs and their Spokes, with credit lines moving liquidity between them. Point-in-time reads cannot reconstruct that movement; only the logs can.

Task 63 builds the event surface for the deployed V3 Pool and explicitly excludes V4. This task extends that work to V4 and should reuse its module, its signature-string conventions and its topic-filter construction rather than starting a second implementation. It depends on 63 landing first.

Two things are V4-specific and worth attention. Credit-line events at the Hub have no V3 analog — they are the only externally visible record of a Spoke drawing on or restoring Hub liquidity, which is the flow that makes the Hub-and-Spoke design observable at all. And Spoke events carry Spoke-local reserveId rather than an asset address, so a decoded event is not self-describing: resolving an id back to its underlying is part of making the output usable.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Ethereum V4 contracts registered in Onchain.Aave.Contracts and Aave-owned aave-v4 IHub / ISpoke / ITokenizationSpoke event definitions. Establish each signature and indexed layout from that source and prove decoding against real mainnet logs at pinned blocks before deriving any fixture; explorers and third-party ABIs are reference material only.

Dispatch trigger: public API addition with live external-system evidence against the archive node.

task.title: Re-sync the V4 address registry with the deployed surface and stop hardcoding three Hubs
acceptance_criteria: Every AaveV4 entry the address book lists for Ethereum and for Avalanche resolves through this library's public API — Hubs, Spokes and their oracles, Tokenization Spokes, Position Managers, gateways, Treasury Spoke, configurators and the access manager

task.body:
The V4 registry describes a deployment that has moved on twice, and one of the two gaps is structural rather than data.

Verified against the address book on 2026-08-26: the AaveV4Ethereum namespace has grown from 150 entries at commit 10c4e9d (2026-04-16, the snapshot V4_SCOPING.md was built from) to 304 today. That includes a fourth Hub, GLOBAL_DOLLAR_HUB at 0x62d63197660c080236193CA60b70E49A08E90368, two additional Spokes, four additional Tokenization Spokes and their interest-rate strategies. Onchain.Aave.V4.Hub types a hub as :core | :prime | :plus and resolves it through a closed case, so the fourth Hub is not merely missing from the registry — it cannot be named. Opening that up is the substance of this task; the rest is data.

Second: V4 is no longer Ethereum-only. It deployed to Avalanche (chainId 43114) on 2026-07-15 with 73 entries — one Core Hub, Main / Forex / AVAX-Correlated Spokes with their oracles, seven Tokenization Spokes, the full Position Manager set including both gateways, and a Treasury Spoke. The contract kind labels are identical to Ethereum's, so no new registry shape is needed. Both @v4_addresses and @v4_tokenization_spokes are already keyed by network, and address/2, v4_contracts/1 and v4_tokenization_spoke/3 are network-generic — adding a network is additive data. The one function that would silently omit it is networks/0, which walks only the V3 map.

Two documentation claims are now false and are load-bearing for other sessions: V4_SCOPING.md and the v0.4.0 CHANGELOG entry both state V4 is Ethereum-mainnet-only, and a task in the aave_sim repo cites that claim as its reason to exclude V4 from multi-chain work. Also note the address book repo has been transferred from the bgd-labs org to aave-dao; the raw URL in CLAUDE.md still resolves, but the recipe should name the canonical org.

Upstream also renamed some keys without changing addresses (ETHERFI_E_SPOKE became ETHERFI_ESPOKE, and price-feed keys gained a _SPOKE infix). Our atoms need not mirror upstream naming, but where they were derived from it, keep them resolvable and say which convention this registry follows.

Address book today has only AaveV4Ethereum and AaveV4Avalanche. The ether.fi Cash instance on Optimism is a DAO-licensed whitelabel and is not in safe.csv; Base V4 lending is announced, not deployed. Both are out of this task — see V4_DEPLOYMENTS.md.

AUTHORITY: the address book at aave-dao/aave-address-book (safe.csv, the AaveV4Ethereum and AaveV4Avalanche namespaces) for the address set, and a live read against the deployed contracts for proof that a registered address is the contract we think it is. Explorers, blog posts and this repo's existing V4_SCOPING.md snapshot are reference material only.

Dispatch trigger: the library's stated coverage disagrees with deployed reality on a money surface, and the fix needs live external-system evidence.

Base V4 and Aerodrome
Re-syncing AaveV4Ethereum / AaveV4Avalanche — Task 69
task.body:
Open decision (default unless observation contradicts it): key this instance as network: :optimism. V3 already uses :optimism for the V3 pool; V4 lives in a separate map so that does not collide. Switch to a named instance key (e.g. :etherfi_cash) only if a second V4 deployment on Optimism is already listed in the address book or an AIP — one V4 per chain is the default.

ether.fi Cash is a live Aave V4 market that this library cannot name. It is not a Spoke on Ethereum Core Hub (that is v4_etherfi_spoke, weETH→WETH e-Mode, already registered). It is a DAO-licensed, EtherFi-operated whitelabel on OP Mainnet: one Liquidity Hub (Cash Hub), one Spoke at launch (Cash Spoke), borrow-whitelisted to Cash cardholders, isolated from every other Aave market. Stani called it the first externally managed V4 deployment. Third-party figures as of 2026-08-26 put it around $249M deposits / $20M borrows, the #2 V4 market by deposits.

Premise verified 2026-08-26 against aave-dao/aave-address-book safe.csv: there is no AaveV4Optimism namespace. Task 69's authority is that file, so Cash is out of 69 on purpose. Landscape and sources: V4_DEPLOYMENTS.md.

This task is only reachable after 69 because Onchain.Aave.V4.Hub currently types a hub as :core | :prime | :plus. Adding :cash (or whatever the instance is called) onto that closed set repeats the Global Dollar failure. 69 opens the type; this task is then additive registry data plus live evidence.

Do not invent addresses. Observe them from the executed AIP / Optimism explorer / a live eth_call that proves the contract is a Hub, then register what was seen. Previews, blogs and V4_DEPLOYMENTS.md figures are reference material, not the address set.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Optimism instance itself (eth_call at a pinned block) plus the Aave governance AIP/ARFC that authorized it (https://governance.aave.com/t/arfc-deploy-a-dedicated-aave-v4-whitelabel-instance-fully-managed-by-etherfi-on-op-mainnet-to-power-ether-fi-cash/25314). The address book is not authority here — it does not list this instance.

Dispatch trigger: the library's stated V4 coverage disagrees with a live deployed market on a money surface, and the fix needs live external-system evidence against a source that is not the DAO address book.
